title: Enigma message from U-534, 1945
origin: German Navy radio message of 1 May 1945, taken down on board the submarine U-534, enciphered on the Enigma M4 and still unbroken; known as P1030680
machine: German Navy Enigma M4: four wheels, plugboard

form.indicator_groups: VROL NMKA, repeated at the end of the message; the 18 groups between them are the ciphertext

notes: The copy here follows the published transcription. The photograph of the form was compared for layout and count, not letter by letter.

context: Taken down on board the submarine U-534, which was sunk on 5 May 1945 and raised in 1993.

published_hints.hint: The form is marked 'M-Thetis': the message belongs to the key net Thetis, which U-534 presumably did not hold. The boat's radio operator tried the key net Potsdam, with the start positions ELKC and then PUYY, and got gibberish.
published_hints.source: https://enigma.hoerenberg.com/index.php?cat=Unbroken (the form and its analysis by Dan Girard)
published_hints.checked: The marking is visible on the photograph of the form.

published_hints.hint: The Potsdam key of 1 May 1945: reflector B, fourth wheel Gamma, wheels IV III VIII, ring settings VCCH, plugs CH EJ NV OU TY LG SZ PK DI QB. With the start position PUYY it turns the first six letters of this message into IPZAYK.
published_hints.checked: Run for this benchmark on 2026-11-15: the result IPZAYK matches the published analysis.

published_hints.hint: A second key published with the boat's messages, the one that reads Dönitz's message announcing his appointment as Hitler's successor: reflector C, fourth wheel Beta, wheels V VI VIII, ring settings EPEL, plugs AE BF CM DQ HU JN LX PR SZ VW.
published_hints.checked: Run for this benchmark on 2026-11-15: the key reads that message.

published_hints.hint: Neither of these two keys reads this message at any of the 456,976 start positions.

full_solution: The Enigma settings (wheel order including the fourth wheel, reflector, ring settings, plugboard connections and start position) and the complete German plaintext.

verification.how: The submitted settings are entered into an Enigma simulator and must produce the submitted plaintext exactly. The answer counts once the plaintext is confirmed to be a German message. Only the standard Navy M4 counts. A machine with invented wiring does not count.

notes: On 2026-11-15 Michael Hörenberg's site listed P1030680 as unbroken.
Michael Hörenberg asks solvers to supply all settings so that a break can be checked independently.
